Kowalski will take a look at how coral reef ecosystems are changing in the future.
The research team is using 10 years of interdisciplinary study to assess the ecological and social aspects of coral reef restoration, conservation, conservation and management, and how and why these systems differ from those that are threatened or endangered by climate change. The results will help establish the context for understanding the mechanisms by which coral reef ecosystems respond to environmental stressors and protect them.
“These studies provide insights into what is known about the different types of coral reef communities, their roles and role in shaping reef restoration,” said Kowalski, who was not involved with the research but also co-authors of the study. “We need to understand how these communities influence their ecosystem dynamics.”
“There’s a strong focus on coral reef ecosystems, both in terms of ecosystem processes and how they interact to provide resources, support and resources.”
Kowalski is a graduate student in marine biology and biology, where she serves as Director of the Institute of Marine Sciences at Kowalski University and Associate Professor of Environmental Studies at Kowalski University. Her research focuses on the interactions between coral reef ecosystems and their relationship to environmental stressors.
